steps: Check fireplace & chimney
Masonry wood-burning fireplace; chimney 15' minimum from the hearth. Sweep and inspect, and repair cracks or loose mortar before installing.

The insert goes into a masonry wood-burning fireplace built to NFPA 211 or applicable codes; the installation conforms to CAN/CSA-B365. Never a makeshift or temporary installation.

  • Chimney height (from hearth): 15' (minimum).
  • Fireplace and chimney must be suitable for wood burning: check for creosote or other obstructions; have the chimney swept and inspected.
  • Inspect for cracks, loose mortar or other defects and complete repairs before installing.
  • Do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance.
Note: the rating label (p. 3) and p. 19 say to install this insert in a masonry fireplace only, not a factory-built one; the clearance text on p. 18 refers to installation "into a masonry or factory built fireplace."
Prepare the fireplace
Lock the damper open or remove it. Don't remove bricks or mortar; fasten the supplied metal tag to the back wall if the fireplace was modified.

The existing fireplace damper is locked open or removed completely.

Do not remove bricks or mortar from the existing fireplace. Exception: masonry or steel, including the damper plate, may come out of the smoke shelf and adjacent damper frame if needed for a chimney liner, provided that doesn't weaken the fireplace and chimney or reduce protection for combustibles below the National Building Code.

If the fireplace was modified for the insert, fasten the supplied metal tag to its back wall.

The insert is heavy: install with two people, and protect the hearth with cardboard or a heavy blanket.
Run the liner
Measure from the top of the chimney flue to the hearth floor, feed the stainless steel liner down through the damper area and fit a stove-to-liner adapter. Full liner required in Canada.

Full flue liner (required in Canada)

Continuous liner from the insert's flue collar to the top of the chimney, meeting the class 3 requirements of CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640. Measure from the top of the existing chimney flue to the floor of the hearth, allowing extra for flashing and rain cap. Feed the liner from the top, through the damper area into the fireplace cavity, and attach a "stove to liner" adapter per the liner manufacturer's instructions.

Direct flue connection (permitted only in the USA)

Measure from the top of the first chimney flue liner tile to the top of the insert, allowing extra to insert into the flue tile. Feed the liner through the damper area into the first flue tile, attach the adapter and seal where the liner passes through the chimney throat. A clean-out door may be required under local codes. Then follow full-liner steps 3-9.

Pacific Energy highly recommends a full liner as the safest installation: the insert drafts correctly, avoiding difficult start-ups and smoking out the door.
Fit the flue collar
The flue collar is packaged in the stove. Attach it to the liner adapter with three stainless screws, caulk the connections with high temp stove cement and check the gasket.
Remove trim, plate & baffle
Lift and pull off the front trim, remove the backing plate (two T20 Torx screws each side), then remove the baffle.

1. Front trim: lift up on each side, then pull it toward you to release the tabs.
  2. Backing plate: remove the two screws (T20 Torx) on each side, pull toward you and lift off.
  3. Baffle (p. 13): slide the ceramic baffle board toward the front and remove the retaining pin at the back of the firebox, just under the baffle. Lift the baffle off the baffle supply tube, move it to one side and tilt it to drop it out. You may need to remove the opposite brick rail: take out the brick under it, then lift the rail up and inward off its locating pins.

Inspect the gasket between baffle and supply tube while it is out; if necessary, replace it with Gasket, 2" Baffle Tube, 10 pack (80000356).

The manual prints this part number as 80000365 on p. 13; the parts list on p. 31 has no 80000365 and lists Gasket, 2" Baffle Tube, 10 pack as 80000356.

The flue gas agitator is pre-installed and should not need handling; do not operate with it removed (p. 15).
Set, level & connect
Push the insert in and level it with the rear adjustment legs. Pull the flue collar down through the flue opening with the tool provided, fit the clamps and nuts, center and tighten.

Push the unit into the fireplace and level it with the rear adjustment legs to suit the hearth configuration; adjustment legs are located in the bottom, sides, front and rear of the insert. If the fireplace is lower than the hearth, prop the unit up and thread the supplied bolts into the threaded inserts under the sides toward the rear, set to the depth of the drop (p. 17).

Reach through the flue opening and pull down on the flue collar with the tool provided until the bolts pass through the mounting holes in the flue opening. Install the clamps and nuts, center the collar on the opening and tighten the nuts.

Baffle back in: the liner procedure (p. 20) removes the baffle but never lists re-installing it. Do not operate with the baffle assembly, tubes or insulation removed. Re-install it in reverse order, with the two blanket pieces tight against the side rails and the ceramic board pushed back tight against the baffle (p. 13).
Flash & cap the chimney
Measure, trim and shape a chimney top flashing with a 1" to 1-1/2" overlap on each side, seat it firmly on the flue tile and attach a rain cap (a storm collar is optional).
Combustion air
Outside air: swap the ash clean-out cover for a rodent screen, keep the air inlet uncovered and seal the surround. Otherwise air is drawn from the room through the front.

Consult local building codes on combustion air supply.

  1. Outside air supply: remove the cover from the ash clean-out in the existing fireplace and put a rodent screen in its place. Install the insert without covering the opening of the air inlet. When finished, seal the surround to the fireplace and anywhere else air may enter, so combustion air is drawn from outside into the intake on the bottom of the appliance.
  2. Room air supply: combustion air is drawn from the room through the front of the unit.
Stove won't burn? The troubleshooting chart says to check the outside air supply for obstruction and that the room air cover is removed.
Power
Plug into a properly grounded outlet that takes a three-pronged plug. Don't route the cord under the unit or against hot or sharp surfaces; it can exit left or right.

Blower rating 120V, 60 Hz, 2.2 A on p. 19 and p. 23; the rating label (p. 3) gives 115V, 60HZ, 1.2 AMP (see Electrical). Don't cut or remove the grounding prong. Follow local codes, or CSA C22.2 (Canada) and ANSI/NFPA 70 (USA).

Moving the cord to the left side (p. 24)

  1. Remove the front trim, the blower speed control knob (supplied Allen key) and the backing plate; disconnect the leads to the rocker switch.
  2. Remove the two screws (Torx T20) holding the electrical box and the wiring cover under the ash shelf.
  3. Remove the strain relief from the right side of the wiring cover, re-route the cord through the left-side hole and re-install the strain relief with pliers.
  4. Remount the wire cover and electrical box, then the backing plate (reconnect the rocker switch leads), the knob and the front trim.
Backing plate, switch & trim
Fit the backing plate with the five screws provided, then the blower speed knob and the rocker switch; hang the front trim with its tabs fully engaged.

1. Attach the backing plate to the mounting brackets on the casing sides with the five screws provided.
  2. Install the blower speed control knob.
  3. Connect the two wires from the right side of the power supply box to the rocker switch assembly; secure the switch to the backing plate with two screws.
  4. Line up the hooks on the back of the front trim with the locking slots in the trim mounting brackets (either side of the firebox, between the blower bracket and the door). Push the trim in, then slide it down to engage the hooks.

Optional battery back-up (11490005, p. 25-26)

Remove the front trim, connect the battery box to the plug on the control board, place the batteries in the box, set it on the outside edge of the backing plate with the wires facing down, and re-install the front trim.

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Never use chemicals or any other volatile liquid to start a fire. Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine.

  1. Move the air control to High, all the way to the left. Open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the centre of the firebox. Crisscross several pieces of small, dry kindling over it, then add a few pieces of large kindling on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open a crack, about 1/2" (13mm) to 1" (25mm), until the kindling is fully engulfed in flame. Never leave the stove unattended with the door open.
  4. Once the kindling is fully engulfed, add a few small pieces of wood. Close the door.
  5. When a good bed of coals has formed and the wood has charred, carry on with normal burning.
Your first 2-3 fires bake on the paint. Keep the room well ventilated: open all windows and doors, because the smoke and fumes can bother some people. Follow the Stove Bright (Forrest Paint) sheet that came with your stove. Smoke detectors may go off more often while the paint cures; don't disconnect them.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
The air control sits beneath the ash lip at the front. Facing the insert, push it right for Low and left for High. The middle is about Medium, and any spot in between works.

High: lighting and fresh wood

After adding wood, run on High for about 10 - 15 minutes, or until the wood is fully charred. Drier wood chars faster. Don't run on High for long periods: you risk over-firing.

Low: overnight and long burns

Char the wood completely on the maximum setting first, then slowly turn the control down to Low. Unsplit logs are best overnight. Never try an overnight burn with green or wet wood.

Adding wood

  1. Set the air control to High and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly. This keeps smoke from puffing out.
  3. Load logs parallel to the front of the stove with space for air between them. Never stack them so high that opening the door becomes hazardous.

After an overnight burn: rake the hot embers toward the front, add a couple of dry, split logs and close the door. Set the air to High; the logs should catch within a few minutes. Once they've charred, reset the air control.

For a clean fire, add small loads (two or three logs) and leave the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes after loading.

wood.title: Choosing and testing wood
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood generally burns more efficiently and cleaner than softwood or freshly cut wood.

  • Season wood for six months or more. Store it under cover, away from open flame or heat sources.
  • Logs can be up to 18 inches long; 16-17 inches is ideal.
  • Wet wood smoulders, makes lots of smoke and creosote, gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.
Maker's website: Log Size (Recommended) 16"; Log Size (Maximum) 17".

Test a piece

Put a large piece on a good, large bed of coals. Burning on more than one side within one minute: dry. Turns black and lights within three minutes: damp. Sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes: soaked, so don't burn it. A moisture meter can confirm.

Never burn

Salt water wood, treated wood, wet, green or unseasoned wood, coal or charcoal, garbage, solvents, lawn clippings or yard waste, railroad ties, manure or animal remains, anything containing rubber (tires included), plastic or asbestos, construction or demolition debris, waste petroleum products, paints, paint thinners, asphalt products, paper products, cardboard, plywood or particleboard. Burning these materials may release toxic fumes, or make the heater ineffective and cause smoke.

Note: The do-not-burn list (p. 6) includes wet, green and unseasoned wood, and p. 8 says to burn natural wood only, dry and well seasoned. p. 8 also says that if you feel it is necessary to burn wet or unseasoned wood, do so only with the air inlet set open enough to maintain a good strong fire and fairly high chimney temperatures, and not to attempt an overnight burn with green or wet wood. Wet wood can cause up to a 25% drop in heater output and adds significantly to creosote buildup.
Salt water wood and garbage contain chlorides that quickly destroy metal and void the warranty. Never barbecue in the insert: fuels like charcoal can make large amounts of carbon monoxide, an odourless gas that can kill.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when the stove is cold, using fireplace glass cleaner.

  • Don't use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape with anything that could scratch the glass.
  • Don't slam the door or knock the glass. Check that no logs stick out before you close it.
  • Clean the plated door with mild soap and water only. Abrasive cleaners void the warranty.

What the deposit tells you

A light brown, dusty film that wipes off easily usually means good combustion, dry wood and a fairly clean chimney. A black, greasy deposit that's hard to remove comes from wet or green wood and burning too slowly. That deposit is building up at least as fast in your chimney.

Cracked or broken glass must be replaced before you use the stove. Get 10-1/2" x 16-1/2" x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer. Don't substitute any other type.

blower.title: Blowers & power outages
blower.html:
The insert has twin variable-speed circulating air blowers, run by a rocker switch and a fan speed control.

AutomaticRocker switch to Off, then pick a speed. The blowers start once the insert reaches operating temperature and stop after the fire is out and it has cooled.
ManualRocker switch to On, then pick a speed. This bypasses the temperature switch.

With the air control on "L" (pushed to the far right), run the blowers on Low. Above "L", any speed is fine.

Vacuum the blowers at least every six months to clear dust and debris. Reaching them means taking off the decorative surround; disconnect power before servicing.

If the power goes out

With the optional battery back-up box installed, the insert stays fully functional. Without it, the insert still runs within safe and certified limits: you control the fire with the manual air control at the front.

ash.title: Emptying the ashes
ash.html:
Take ashes out only when the heater is cold.

  1. Wait until the ashes are 3" to 4" deep and the fire has burned down and cooled.
  2. Remove the extra ash, but leave a bed about 1" deep on the firebox floor. It helps keep a hot charcoal bed.
  3. Keep the front of the firebox clear of heavy ash. That's where boost air for the fire comes in, and ash buildup blocks it.

Storing the ashes

  • Use a metal container with a tight-fitting lid.
  • Set the closed container on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn.
  • If you bury or spread the ashes, keep them in the closed container until every cinder has cooled completely.
  • Don't put any other waste in that container.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow fires give off tar and vapours that condense in the cool chimney as creosote. If it ignites, it burns extremely hot: temperatures inside the chimney can exceed 2000°F (1100°C).

  • Have the chimney and connector inspected at least once every two months in the heating season. Remove creosote once it reaches 3 mm or more.
  • Until you learn your pattern, check daily. Weekly cleaning may be needed in mild weather; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.
  • Burn dry wood, don't turn the air down too soon after loading, and never burn trash, cardboard or Christmas tree limbs.
Before the chimney is swept, remove the top grill (two screws) and pull the flue thermocouple guide out as far as it goes, so the thermocouple tip is out of the flue opening. Push it back in afterward.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting from the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

What to do

  1. Get everyone ready to leave, and meet at an agreed place outside.
  2. Close the air inlet on the stove.
  3. Call the fire department. Keep a fire extinguisher handy.
  4. Afterward, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks before the next fire.

care.title: Routine checks
care.html:
Check these parts for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and excessive warping.

WeeklyFirebrick (cracks); door gasket (sagging, placement, damage)
MonthlyBrick rails and their tabs, air riser tube at the back of the firebox, back of the airwash chamber, baffle locking pin, baffle tubes
When the chimney is cleanedTop baffle board and blanket, baffle, top heat shield and bolts, baffle gasket, brick rails, manifold
  • Some baffle warping, up to 1/4", is normal. Replace the baffle if it warps more, cracks or breaks.
  • Replace broken or missing firebricks; burning without them can be hazardous.
  • The door gasket needs only light pressure to seal. Inspect it and replace it when needed with the kit from your dealer.
  • Use only materials supplied by the manufacturer.

Door gasket part numbers: the replacement kit, which comes with instructions, is part# 80000156 (p. 11). The parts list numbers the gasket itself, Gasket, Door, NEO 1.6, as 80000670 (p. 31).

Tell your dealer about any damage. Running the stove with broken parts can damage other parts and may void your warranty.

safety.title: Safety & over-firing
safety.html:
• The insert is hot while it burns. Keep children, clothing and furniture away; touching it can burn skin.
  • Hot glass will burn you. Don't touch it until it has cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning, and open it only to add wood.
  • Never use gasoline-type lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or similar liquids to start or freshen a fire. Keep them well away from the heater.
  • Burn directly on the firebricks. Don't use a grate or andirons.
  • Don't store wood or other combustibles within the clearances or in the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended in the area of the heater.
  • Make sure everyone in your family knows how to run it safely and what to do in a chimney fire.

Signs of over-firing

A glowing red top or vent pipe means the heater is being pushed past its design. That can permanently damage the heater and chimney, is hazardous if not corrected, and may void the warranty. Don't run on High for long periods. An uncontrollable burn or glowing red parts can also mean too much chimney draft.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
The warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years), parts onlyPorcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage only, not impact), plating, firebox and baffle
3 year comprehensive, parts and laborAny part found defective, from the date of purchase, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Labor under the lifetime coverage.
  • Firebox rails and heat shields (excluded from the lifetime warranty).
  • Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets.
  • Misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification.

Excessive draft, heating too large an area, or contaminated fuel (high sodium, plastics, chemicals) may void it. So can tampering with the air control, burning salt water wood or garbage, over-firing, and abrasive cleaners on the plated door.

Making a claim

Contact your dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, the model name and the serial number. The serial number is on the product certification label or the cover of your installation manual. You can register the product at pacificenergy.net/register.

specPerf.title: Emissions, efficiency & output
specPerf.html:
EPA certified emissions1.6 grams per hour
HHV tested efficiency75%
LHV tested efficiency82%
EPA BTU output13,494 to 23,186 btu/hr.
CO emissions1.4 grams per minute
Maker's website: Heat Output (Cord Wood) 56,000 BTU.

Meets the 2020 EPA crib wood emission limits (Method 28R). Efficiencies are weighted averages tested to CSA B415; the BTU range uses the low and high EPA burn rates on Douglas Fir dimensional lumber. The rating text rounds it to 13,500 to 23,200 Btu/hr.

Listed solid wood fuel fireplace insert, certified to CAN/ULC 628 / UL1482 (Intertek, C# 4001507). Rating label: bottom, back corner of the side casing on the door catch side.

Factory-set low burn rate. Altering it, or operating against the manual's instructions, is against federal regulations. No alteration or modification of the combustion air control assembly is permitted.

specFuel.title: Fuel & wood length
specFuel.html:
Maximum wood length18 inches
Ideal wood length16-17 inches
FuelSeasoned cord wood
Maker's website: Log Size (Recommended) 16"; Log Size (Maximum) 17".

Solid fuel (cordwood) only. Load parallel to the stove front with space for air between logs, directly on the firebrick: no grate or andirons. Wood air dried (seasoned) six months or more.

specLiner.title: Flue, liner & draft
specLiner.html:
Flue collar6" I.D., removable
CanadaFull liner, collar to chimney top, class 3, CAN/ULC-S635 or CAN/ULC-S640
USALiner conforming to UL-1777, or direct flue connection assembly
Chimney height (from hearth)15' (minimum)

Do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance. A direct flue connection (USA only) needs a seal in the chimney throat, and local codes may require a clean-out door.

Too much draft: excessive temperatures, an uncontrollable burn or glowing red parts. Too little: back puffing, a plugged chimney, smoke leaking at appliance and connector joints.

specHearth.title: Hearth & ember protection
specHearth.html:
Fireplace hearth (p. 16)

The non-combustible masonry hearth must extend 16" in front and 8" beyond each side of the existing fireplace opening. Rating label: install only on a non-combustible hearth under the unit, extending 16" (406 mm) in front of the fireplace opening face.

Ember protection

Combustible flooring in front of the insert needs non-combustible material extending:

USA16" to the firing side (from the glass), 8" to each side of the door opening
Canada18" to the firing side (from the glass), 8" to each side of the unit

Codes: CAN/CSA-B365 (Canada), NFPA 211 (USA). Figure 12 shows ember protection as a dimensioned drawing.

review.notes: One manual (100006918, 080125-36, 36 pp.). Matches catalog: 1.6 g/hr, 75% HHV, EPA 2020, 6 in. flue collar, twin blowers, regular 37 x 26 3/4 / oversized 46 x 30 surround, black or stainless front trim; btu_output_epa 23200 matches the rating text. Not in the manual, so not checked or used: firebox volume, heating area, burn time, catalog btu_output_max (manual gives only the EPA range), blower cfm, catalytic or not, ACMS, view/glass area (manual gives only the replacement glass size), knife-edge seal, stainless baffle. No battery type or count for the optional battery box. Figures not transcribed: insert dimensions (Fig. 7, p. 14; only its A/B surround table used), minimum fireplace opening (Fig. 11, p. 16), ember protection drawing (Fig. 12, p. 17; its 20 1/4 / 18 1/4 callouts and an '18" / 406mm' label don't match the label's 457 mm), clearance drawing (Fig. 13, p. 18; a 34 3/8 / 840mm callout is unexplained), wiring diagram (p. 23), firebrick layout (p. 28), parts diagram (p. 32). Text errors: p. 2 intro calls the unit 'VISTA INSERT LE' and Fig. 24 says 'Vista Insert LE2'; cross-references are off (p. 19 'see page 12' for fireplace size is p. 16; p. 16 'Figure 7' is Fig. 11; p. 18 'Figure 12' is Fig. 13; p. 24 'Fig. #9/#10' are Figs. 17/18). Not flagged as conflicts: backing plate screws (p. 20 two T20 Torx each side vs p. 24 five screws provided); BTU range rounding on p. 3 (both values shown). The full-liner sequence (p. 20) removes the baffle but never re-installs it; step5 drawer points to p. 13. Warranty printed as 'LTD Lifetime Coverage (10 years)'. Bilingual label only; no French-only or scrambled text. No code table, so codes empty. Pages 34-35 blank. Website (Oct 12): Maker's website notes added for log size (specFuel, and the owner wood drawer) and Heat Output (Cord Wood) 56,000 BTU (specPerf, after the manual's EPA BTU output). website.json prints no minimum output, so the btu_output_min mismatch (catalog 12315) has no website figure to quote. Website rows the manual doesn't cover, so skipped: Firebox Size 1.4 cu.ft., Glass Viewing Area 147 sq.in., Blowers 2x80 cfm. Efficiency 75%, emissions 1.6, flue outlet 6", EPA 2020 and east-west loading match the manual.
